reviews.reasoning: Numbering re-derived, not inherited: Ps 141 is an identity psalm (ps_lib.web_to_mt(141,1) returns (141,1); verse_map_web records Ps.141.0 as mt 'inside Ps.141.1'), so the opening row's title ref web:Ps.141.0 = oshb:Ps.141.1 is arithmetically correct and pre-ruled in form; citation_sweep.py reports 0 problems for this row. The row's single original-language citation collates at tier byte against oshb:Ps.141.2 (collate.py, quote spliced file-to-file), and its WEB companions at web:Ps.141.1, web:Ps.141.2 and web:Ps.141.3 are verbatim (check_web_quotes.py: 22 quotes checked across the cluster, 0 flags). Disclosure obligations re-derived from the inventories: pmarks_Ps.json holds 0 selah, 0 ketiv/qere, 0 inverted-nun, 0 suspended-letter and 0 puncta entries anywhere in Ps 141, so the only seg-layer object in this span is paseq (2 segs at MT Ps.141.4, single-witness), which the row neither claims nor denies - no gap. Tiling inside Ps 141 is exact across 1-4 / 5-7 / 8-10 (check_tiling.py reports no gap, overlap or order problem within the range). The seam at 141:4|5 itself is defensible and I do not contest it: MT 141:5 takes a third-person subject and leaves the petition register. What is missing is disclosure of a byte-true referential chain that runs straight across that seam - filed below. Two observations not filed as defects. (a) MT 141:2 juxtaposes prayer and incense with no comparative particle; the word 'simile' is a property of the WEB rendering “like incense” (web:Ps.141.2), not of the bytes - contrast MT 143:6's explicit כְּאֶֽרֶץ עֲיֵפָ֖ה, which does carry the comparative kaf (tier byte). The row's claim that the Hebrew 'grounds the incense simile' is loose rather than wrong. (b) MT 141:4 carries no 2ms pronominal suffix and no vocative, so the row's 'continuous second-person imperative address to Yahweh' is thinner at v4 than at vv1-3; the staged extract has no morphology layer, so the reading rests on WEB's rendering plus the negative particle, which is a legitimate but weaker warrant than the row's 'high' confidence implies.

challenges.claim: The row asserts vv1-4 run without a topic change until the turn at web:Ps.141.5, but a byte-true 3mp referential chain runs continuously across the row's own 141:4|5 seam and is left undisclosed.
challenges.evidence: MT 141:4 names the antecedent אֶת אִישִׁ֥ים פֹּֽעֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן and immediately suffixes it בְּמַנְעַמֵּיהֶֽם; MT 141:5 ends בְּרָעוֹתֵיהֶֽם and MT 141:6 carries שֹׁפְטֵיהֶ֑ם, the same 3mp suffix. All four runs were spliced from verse_map_oshb.json and collate at tier byte (collate.py --json). Digit-bearing sweeps, unit named: sweep.py --skel over the form of MT 141:5 returns 1 verse in Psalms (MT Ps.141.5) and over the form of MT 141:6 returns 1 verse in Psalms (MT Ps.141.6). Ps 141 is an identity psalm so MT and WEB numbering coincide throughout. The wicked are therefore the continuing topic across the seam - WEB keeps the possessive at web:Ps.141.4 (“their delicacies”) and drops it at web:Ps.141.5 (“evil deeds”), which is why the English reads as a cleaner break than the Hebrew is. Cure (one edit, installed on both rows of the 141:4|5 seam pair): re-state the warrant as a speech-act turn rather than a topic change, and disclose the suffix chain.

reviews.reasoning: Two of the row's three signals hold on re-derivation. WEB does render web:Ps.141.7 as quoted speech with no attributed speaker (verse_map_web's text field opens and closes the verse with WEB's own quotation marks and the only footnote is the Sheol gloss), and no vocative occurs inside vv5-7 in either witness - MT 141:5, 141:6 and 141:7 contain no divine-name token at all, while MT 141:3 and MT 141:8 do. The WEB quotations are verbatim including “Their judges are thrown down by the sides of the rock.” (web:Ps.141.6). The 'medium_low' confidence is honest for this zone and I would keep it. Paseq sits at MT Ps.141.5 (1 seg, single-witness, inventory-cited) and is not claimed either way, so no disclosure gap. The third signal is the load-bearing one and it is false against the bytes, and the row's outside-span citations are not mirrored.

challenges.evidence: MT 141:4 states a plural nominal antecedent, אֶת אִישִׁ֥ים פֹּֽעֲלֵי אָ֑וֶן, and suffixes it in the same verse, בְּמַנְעַמֵּיהֶֽם; MT 141:5 carries the same 3mp suffix at בְּרָעוֹתֵיהֶֽם; MT 141:6's שֹׁפְטֵיהֶ֑ם continues it. Slices spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, all tier byte (collate.py). Ps 141 is identity, so no dual-cite arithmetic is at issue. The chain is therefore unbroken from two verses before the pronoun. The claim most likely arose from the English: WEB keeps the possessive at web:Ps.141.4 (“their delicacies”) but drops the 3mp suffix at web:Ps.141.5, rendering it “evil deeds”. check_universals.py independently flags this signal as a universal claim carrying no adjacent digit-bearing sweep count. The row's honest low-confidence register survives - the connective logic of vv6-7 is genuinely unsettled - but the antecedent premise must be withdrawn or narrowed to 'no antecedent is named inside vv5-7'.

MT 141:8 does reopen direct address, and WEB's “Yahweh, the Lord” (web:Ps.141.8) renders MT's divine-name pair there; the pair is not in the ketiv/qere inventory (pmarks_Ps.json kq holds 0 entries anywhere in Ps 141-143, its nearest entries being MT Ps.140.10, .11 and .13), so no K/Q disclosure is owed and none is claimed. All WEB quotations are verbatim (check_web_quotes.py 0 flags), citation_sweep.py reports 0 problems, and paseq at MT Ps.141.8 (1 seg, single-witness) is unclaimed - no gap. Two observations, neither filed. (a) The snare/net cohesion claim for vv9-10 is right at the image level though the lexemes differ across the two verses, and MT 141:10's net noun carries a 3ms suffix where WEB reads “their own nets” (web:Ps.141.10) - a rendering nuance, not a defect, since the row argues the image and not the morphology. (b) A byte-true datum the row could have used and did not: the workers-of-iniquity phrase recurs at MT Ps.141.4 and MT Ps.141.9 - sweep.py --skel returns 15 verses in Psalms, 2 of them in Ps 141 - bracketing the middle zone and corroborating the three-row shape rather than opposing it. The only defect is a mirror miss.

challenges.claim: In this non-identity psalm the original-language citation oshb:Ps.142.2 carries no WEB arithmetic in observed_substrate_signals[0] and no matching dual pairing in boundary_evidence_refs.

Stated for the record as mitigation, measured rather than estimated: in the rationale field the gap between the end of 'oshb:Ps.142.2' and the start of 'web:Ps.142.1' is 77 characters, so citation_sweep's plus/minus 80-character context window truncates 'web:Ps.142.1' after its first three characters and the substring test fails by 9 characters. The rationale is therefore materially compliant in the preferred in-field form; the real gaps are observed_substrate_signals[0], which contains no web: ref at all, and the refs array. Cure: add web:Ps.142.1 = oshb:Ps.142.2 to boundary_evidence_refs, which discharges both.

reviews.reasoning: Ps 143 is an identity psalm (ps_lib.web_to_mt(143,1) returns (143,1); verse_map_web records Ps.143.0 as mt 'inside Ps.143.1'), so the title ref web:Ps.143.0 = oshb:Ps.143.1 is correct and citation_sweep.py reports 0 problems. Both WEB quotes are verbatim. I would keep the 2|3 seam: MT 143:1-2 is petition throughout - three 2ms imperatives in v1, then v2 continues with a conjunctive waw plus negative particle and the 2ms suffix עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ - whereas MT 143:3 switches to perfect-tense third-person report of the enemy. A 2-verse strophe is short against the strategy's roughly 4-8-verse guidance, but the register break is byte-real and the row policy is elastic, so I do not contest the span on granularity alone. Two observations, neither filed as a defect. (a) This row's rejected_alternative characterises web:Ps.143.3's causal particle as opening a new causal ground, while the row on the far side of the very same seam characterises it as continuing web:Ps.143.2's ground; under the seam-pair rule one edit should settle which reading stands, since both particles are the same lexeme. (b) The row cites the servant word at v2 but not its return at MT 143:12, עַבְדֶּֽךָ (tier byte) - sweep.py --skel returns 27 verses in Psalms carrying that skeleton, exactly 2 of them in Ps 143, MT Ps.143.2 and MT Ps.143.12 - which is the psalm's strongest inclusio and would strengthen both this row and the closing row. Paseq at MT Ps.143.1 (1 seg, single-witness) is unclaimed, no gap; no selah anywhere in the span-relevant set. The one filed defect is register.

challenges.claim: device_notes carries a positional, file-order reference to other rows, which the book's register rule bans in row prose.

The book strategy's §10 register rule bans positional row references and file-order talk in row prose EVER and requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored. The defect is in this one variation order of the mandated parent-grouping sentence, not in the sentence's purpose: the sibling variations in the same cluster avoid it entirely ('One composition, Psalm 141, parents this row set.' and 'Psalm 142's single row constitutes its entire parent grouping.'), so a position-free reformulation is available without changing the fact asserted.

challenges.claim: The row's only stated warrant for closing at 143:6 is the selah, which the book's binding policy forbids as a boundary driver on its own, and the row carries no back-seam ref at all.
challenges.evidence: The rationale ends 'closing with selah at web:Ps.143.6', and the rejected_alternative's only reason for not stopping earlier is that vv5-6 run 'through to their own selah close at web:Ps.143.6'. The strategy's §2d states selah is at MOST tier-3-like corroboration of a strophe close and NEVER a boundary driver alone, and §6 permits selah-corroborated closes only WITH an independent driver. boundary_evidence_refs holds a single entry, web:Ps.143.2 - the front seam - where every other row in this cluster carries both seams. The independent driver exists in the bytes and is simply unstated: MT 143:7 opens מַ֘הֵ֤ר עֲנֵ֨נִי יְהוָה֮, an imperative plus vocative that reopens the 2ms petition register which MT 143:3-6 had left for perfect-tense report and first-person description, the description closing at כְּאֶֽרֶץ עֲיֵפָ֖ה immediately before סֶֽלָה in MT 143:6. All three runs spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, tier byte (collate.py). Cure: add web:Ps.143.7 to boundary_evidence_refs, name the imperative-plus-vocative reopening as the driver, and demote selah to corroboration.

reviews.reasoning: The textual work in this row is clean: both original-language citations collate at tier byte against oshb:Ps.143.8 and oshb:Ps.143.10 (collate.py --json, spliced file-to-file), the WEB companions at web:Ps.143.8 and web:Ps.143.10 are verbatim, Ps 143 is identity so no dual-cite arithmetic is owed, and citation_sweep.py reports 0 problems for the row. The cohesion claim is byte-true as well - MT 143:7, 143:8, 143:9 and 143:10 each open or carry 2ms imperatives addressed to Yahweh, an uninterrupted petition sequence across all four verses - and the 6|11 span edges match the seams the neighbouring rows argue. The two defects are both in the disclosure layer, and they compound: the row states an absence that the inventories contradict, and stays silent about the one selah in the psalm even though that selah sits on the row's own front seam and its ref is already in the row's refs array.

challenges.claim: The row's span-relevant set contains the psalm's only selah, at its front seam, and the row discloses none.

Running check_marks.py's own span-relevant helper over this row returns a span-relevant selah set of exactly one entry, MT Ps.143.6, while the row's prose contains 0 occurrences of the word selah. The strategy's §2d requires every row whose span-relevant set - front seam plus interior plus end - contains selah to disclose every instance, and the campaign rule is that symmetry completion is a sweep, not a spot fix. The verse text itself ends סֶֽלָה (oshb:Ps.143.6, tier byte), so this is quotable verse text in both witnesses, not a seg-layer object. check_marks.py does not catch this because its symmetry arm is gated on the row already mentioning selah - reported separately as a toolkit defect, not charged to the row.

Everything else checks out: both WEB quotations are verbatim (check_web_quotes.py 0 flags), no original-language citation is made so no collation or dual-cite question arises, citation_sweep.py reports 0 problems, and the row's span-relevant set carries no selah (the psalm's only selah, MT Ps.143.6, lies four verses upstream of the front seam) so nothing is owed there; paseq at MT Ps.143.10 and MT Ps.143.11 (1 seg each, single-witness) is unclaimed. The closing pointer back to web:Ps.143.1 is apt, though the tighter frame is the servant word at MT 143:2 and MT 143:12, עַבְדֶּֽךָ (tier byte) - sweep.py --skel returns 27 verses in Psalms, exactly 2 of them in Ps 143 - which would give this row a second, byte-true closing warrant.

challenges.claim: The row twice asserts that web:Ps.143.11 opens on the name-formula, but the WEB verse it cites opens on the revival petition; it is the MT verse that is formula-initial.
challenges.evidence: WEB web:Ps.143.11 reads “Revive me, Yahweh, for your name’s sake. In your righteousness, bring my soul out of trouble.” - the formula is the verse's second element, after the imperative and the vocative. MT 143:11 opens לְמַֽעַן שִׁמְךָ֣, and the full opening colon runs לְמַֽעַן שִׁמְךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה תְּחַיֵּ֑נִי, placing the formula before both the vocative and the verb (both runs spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, tier byte). Ps 143 is an identity psalm so web:Ps.143.11 = oshb:Ps.143.11 and no arithmetic is in dispute - only the witness attribution, which appears in rejected_alternative and again in observed_substrate_signals[0]. The underlying signal is sound and in fact stronger than stated: sweep.py --skel over the formula returns 5 verses in Psalms, exactly 1 of them in Ps 143 (MT Ps.143.11), and there it is verse-initial. Cure: attribute the verse-initial position to MT and cite it as oshb:Ps.143.11, or restate the WEB claim as 'carries' rather than 'opens on'.
